subsystems.name: Identity provider
subsystems.role: proves who a user or machine is before anything else happens.

subsystems.name: Policy engine and administrator
subsystems.role: decides, per request, whether this identity on this device may reach this resource now.

subsystems.name: Policy enforcement points
subsystems.role: sit in front of each resource and allow or block traffic on the policy engine's verdict.

subsystems.name: Device posture and inventory
subsystems.role: only known, patched, managed devices are treated as trustworthy.

subsystems.name: Microsegmentation fabric
subsystems.role: splits the internal network so a compromise in one service cannot move freely.

subsystems.name: Telemetry and analytics
subsystems.role: gives the policy engine live evidence and catches behaviour that policy missed.

buildSteps.title: Inventory assets and data flows
buildSteps.detail: Map every user, service, device and the data they touch. Policy cannot be written for systems nobody has catalogued.

buildSteps.title: Give every actor a strong identity
buildSteps.detail: Enrol staff in single sign-on with multi-factor authentication, and issue cryptographic identities to servers, containers and workloads as well as people.

buildSteps.title: Register and assess devices
buildSteps.detail: Enrol laptops and phones in management, install device certificates, and define the minimum patch level and configuration a device needs.

buildSteps.title: Stand up the policy decision point
buildSteps.detail: Deploy a central engine that evaluates identity, device posture and context, and writes rules such as 'finance staff on managed devices, during work hours, for these applications'.

buildSteps.title: Insert enforcement points
buildSteps.detail: Put identity-aware proxies or gateways in front of each application so every request is checked, rather than trusting anything already inside the network.

buildSteps.title: Microsegment the internal network
buildSteps.detail: Replace flat internal routing with per-workload rules and mutual TLS, so east-west traffic is authenticated too.

buildSteps.title: Retire perimeter-only access
buildSteps.detail: Move users off blanket VPN access to per-application, least-privilege, just-in-time connections, keeping break-glass accounts for outages.

buildSteps.title: Instrument and tune continuously
buildSteps.detail: Feed logs and alerts back into policy, tighten rules that prove unnecessary, and rehearse what happens when the identity system itself fails.

prerequisites.why: phishing-resistant factors and device certificates are the root of every trust decision.

prerequisites.tech: Open standards for identity and federation
prerequisites.why: OpenID Connect, SAML and FIDO2/WebAuthn let many vendors' components interoperate.
they are the enforcement points that make per-request checking practical.
short-lived credentials only work if issuance and renewal are automatic.

prerequisites.tech: Legacy and industrial systems that support modern authentication
prerequisites.why: many industrial control, medical and mainframe systems cannot present a modern identity, forcing exceptions.

pathway.milestone: identity-first deployments: single sign-on, universal MFA, per-application access replacing blanket VPN
pathway.unlocks: a big reduction in credential theft and lateral movement.

pathway.milestone: phishing-resistant authentication such as passkeys and hardware security keys as the default, plus device attestation
pathway.unlocks: defence against credential phishing and stolen-session attacks.

pathway.milestone: workload identity and mutual TLS across data centres and clouds
pathway.unlocks: microsegmentation that does not depend on network location.

pathway.milestone: continuous, risk-adaptive policy with automated containment, extended to operational technology
pathway.unlocks: access decisions that tighten in real time when behaviour looks wrong, across factories and critical infrastructure as well as offices.
